extracted.intended_audience: humanities scholars, AI researchers, and prospective applicants to the Schmidt Sciences HAVI grant program
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and program priorities for Schmidt Sciences' Humanities and AI Virtual Institute (HAVI) awards: projects that develop or adapt AI to address problems in archaeology, history, literature and other humanities fields, with emphasis on multimodal/multilingual data, low-resource contexts, and open tools/datasets. The page describes funded project types, methodological goals, and selection process signals for future applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply AI to humanities research
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should develop and apply artificial intelligence to archaeology, history, literature and other humanities disciplines to unlock new understandings of human history and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page framing: "develop and apply artificial intelligence to archaeology, history, literature and other humanities disciplines, seeking to unlock new understandings of human history and culture." Examples: virtual unrolling of scrolls, analyzing film, discovering archaeological sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create new AI models or evolve existing ones for humanities needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Support researchers to create new AI models or evolve existing ones specifically to open new avenues for historical understanding and inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis that off-the-shelf models trained on contemporary large-scale data are insufficient; projects must adapt or build models for humanities-specific modalities and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address domain mismatch (languages, media, scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work must contend with the mismatch between typical AI training data (contemporary data, modern languages, 2D media) and humanities data (ancient/lesser-spoken languages, three-dimensional artifacts, varied materials, small/ambiguous/culture-specific corpora).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page explains these limitations and uses them to motivate projects: e.g., ancient languages, three-dimensional artifacts, small amounts of ambiguous and culture-specific information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal analysis (text, image, audio, 3D, material data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should handle multimodal inputs—combining text, images, soundtracks, 3D imaging, material/chemical imaging and other non-text modalities relevant to humanities objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include film (visual + aural timing), multimodal archives of newspapers/images, imaging of artworks (micro-CT), non-invasive imaging for papyri, and material-property analysis of objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support low-resource and underrepresented languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Train or adapt multilingual models to study manuscripts and texts in low-resource languages (e.g., Tibetan) to reduce overreliance on well-known translations and diminish bias in historical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project example: "Connectivity and Individuality in Textual Traditions" to train multilingual AI models for Asian-language manuscripts; emphasis on under-resourced languages across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary integration with humanistic scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine large-scale computational/AI methods with close humanistic reading and domain expertise so outputs are meaningful for humanities scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit example: combining computational analysis with film scholarship to measure shot types, classify camera movement, disentangle storylines, and relate visual and aural timing; integration into digital humanities labs like Kinolab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-access and open-source outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for producing open-access tools, datasets and models that enable broader use by the scholarly community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several projects commit to releasing open-access tools and datasets (e.g., AI archaeology suite, open-source datasets for printer identification). The program highlights open-access as a deliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toolkits, libraries and reproducible software for scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver practical software/toolkits (for example Python libraries) that humanities scholars can use to study large-scale patterns and structures in multimodal corpora.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an ML toolkit / Python library to find hierarchical structure in multimodal and multilingual data for humanities researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks and evaluation sensitive to historical and cultural context
rubrics_metrics.description: Create benchmarks and evaluation methods that reflect distinct cultural contexts and historical periods so model performance is measured against historically appropriate criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project example: developing benchmarks to ensure AI models can faithfully reflect distinct cultural contexts and historical periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to avoid cultural flattening and preserve contextual nuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop techniques that prevent 'cultural flattening' when AI models analyze multicultural and multimodal historical data, preserving cultural specificity and nuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit project goal: prevent cultural flattening and apply the technique to study emergence of jazz in New Orleans using fragile, multimodal sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovering and restoring damaged or illegible texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI (including reinforcement learning and generative methods) and imaging to decipher, edit, or virtually reconstruct documents that are damaged, faded, torn, or otherwise illegible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reinforcement-learning models to edit damaged manuscripts; virtual unrolling of papyrus scrolls using non-invasive imaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-invasive imaging and 3D surface extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply non-invasive imaging techniques and computational methods to extract information from three-dimensional or fragile artifacts without physically opening or damaging them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project example: 'Meeting the Vesuvius Challenge'—virtual unrolling of papyrus scrolls and extracting complex 3D surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical provenance, material and technical-art-history analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine AI with imaging and material analysis to study how artworks and objects were made, how their materials change over time, and to build predictive frameworks of degradation/restoration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: imaging and AI to study Van Gogh's pigments and build a predictive 'rewind time' framework; integrating 'messy' data in technical art history (material properties + images + text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery and mapping of archaeological and landscape features
rubrics_metrics.description: Use remote sensing, satellite and aerial imagery with AI to find and map historic roadways, field systems, burial grounds, and other archaeological features at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project example: open-access AI archaeology suite using vast data stores of satellite imagery and aerial photography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searchable multimodal archival databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Build searchable, multimodal (text + image) archives and AI-based search methods to surface hidden, veiled, or risky-to-express content (e.g., coded political messaging in historical newspapers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: creating a searchable database of Black newspapers and methods to identify veiled protest and political messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models and datasets for music notation and historic musical expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Create large datasets and models that translate between notation, lyrics, and audio to enable AI understanding of multiple ways music is expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: building a dataset and music translation model for Musica Subtilior to advance musical AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital editions, translation mapping and textual influence studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use generative AI and multilingual methods to perform multidimensional translation and to map influence, transmission, and commentary of texts across languages and millennia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: using generative AI to map influence of texts and their translations, building on resources like the Perseus Digital Repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for legal/historical corpora and tracing idea diffusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Create databases and tools for multilingual, multimodal legal text to scan and detect how legal ideas, statutes, and administrative codes arise and spread over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project example: AI for Understanding the Law and its Evolution—scanning centuries of case law and administrative codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models designed for archival heterogeneity (multiple manuscript copies/discrepancies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle collections where documents exist in multiple handwritten copies with many discrepancies (e.g., medieval papal writings) and enable multilingual, access-friendly interfaces like chatbots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: building a multilingual chatbot for exploring 4th and 5th century papal writings, which exist in multiple discrepant copies in arcane Latin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope across geographies and millennia
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may focus on varied geographic and temporal ranges—from industrial England to Qing-era China to ancient Egypt—demonstrating applicability across diverse historical contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page repeatedly emphasizes range across geographies and millennia as part of program vision and funded projects list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce replicable benchmarks, datasets, and public resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliverables should include reproducible benchmarks, datasets, and public resources that enable experimental approaches to historical questions previously limited to observational evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include benchmarks for cultural/historical reasoning, open datasets for printers' identification, and resources to unlock shorthand and other large corpora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription of historical shorthand and large-scale paleography
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop AI methods to automatically transcribe historical shorthand and other difficult paleographic systems to unlock millions of handwritten pages in archives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project example: decoding historical shorthand to make European archive materials legible to scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and review process involves multiple rounds and external experts
rubrics_metrics.description: The program selects teams after multiple rounds of review by Schmidt Sciences and external experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This signals that applications will be evaluated through staged review and by external peer/expert reviewers.
